primary_direction.title: Mechanism-Guided Adaptive Psychiatry
primary_direction.problem: Complex psychiatric presentations overlap across categories and treatment response varies across people and time; diagnosis-only selection cannot represent active mechanisms, context, or changing response.
primary_direction.hypothesis: A clinician-supervised transdiagnostic model combining symptom dimensions, multimodal mechanisms, and repeated response trajectories will improve treatment matching, calibration, and time-to-effective care.
mechanism: inflammation-associated dysconnectivity in a patient subset
closed-loop-style repeated monitoring under clinical governance
primary_direction.novelty: Links mechanism strata to treatment-specific trajectories and a safe adaptive policy, evaluating utility and fairness rather than biomarker association alone.
primary_direction.expected_result: Prospective emulation and held-out validation will show a calibrated but imperfect gain over diagnosis-only and symptom-only baselines, with subgroup-specific and modality-specific effects.
falsification: No held-out predictive or utility gain over symptom-only baseline.
Mechanism strata fail replication or add no treatment interaction.
Adaptive policy worsens time-to-effective-care or adverse-event burden.
Subgroup calibration or fairness fails predefined thresholds.

handoff_requirements: compare diagnosis-only, symptom-only, and multimodal models
separate association, prediction, clinical utility, and safety
model treatment response as a trajectory
